culture_principles.name: Public mission and customer-impact alignment
culture_principles.description: Bain & Company fit should connect work to the company outcomes and users described in cited public sources.

culture_principles.name: Evidence-backed execution
culture_principles.description: Strong answers should show practical judgment, clear tradeoffs, ownership, and outcomes rather than generic enthusiasm.

culture_principles.name: Candor as a working norm
culture_principles.description: Bain presents candor as the basis of collaboration and pairs teamwork and trust with tolerance for diverging opinions, so direct feedback and open disagreement are expected parts of the work.

culture_principles.name: Results that hold after the engagement
culture_principles.description: Bain says it measures success by clients' success and points to client advocacy, so the lens treats adoption and durable client outcomes as the result rather than the deliverable.

culture_principles.name: Apprenticeship through generalist problem solving
culture_principles.description: Bain describes a coaching and apprenticeship culture with personal champions, formal training, career guidance, and separate consulting, client-delivery expert, and functional tracks.

culture_principles.name: Technology judgment paired with hands-on build
culture_principles.description: Bain describes combining strategy with engineering and change leadership, and staffs teams that include engineers, AI experts, data scientists, and designers alongside strategists.

hiring_signals.signal: Connects decisions to the users, customers, products, or markets named in public company sources.
Uses concrete examples to show ownership, learning, and measurable improvement.
Structures an ambiguous problem into testable parts and states what evidence would change the recommendation.
Shows how the candidate gave and acted on direct feedback inside a team, including disagreement with someone more senior.
Connects analysis to a client decision that was actually adopted, and can explain the adoption mechanism.
Explains the problem structure, the evidence gathered, and why alternative options were rejected, rather than only naming a framework.
Shows how direct feedback or a conflicting viewpoint changed their approach, consistent with Bain's stated tolerance for diverging opinions.
Connects a recommendation to implementation choices, organizational constraints, and whether the client actually adopted the change.
Works through a case-style problem step by step, states assumptions, and updates the answer when new data arrives.

anti_signals.anti_signal: Generic admiration for the company without a concrete role, customer, product, or business mechanism.
anti_signals.risk_reason: Public lens usage should stay grounded in cited source signals and role-relevant evidence.

anti_signals.anti_signal: Reciting a consulting framework by name without showing why it fit this problem or what it excluded.
anti_signals.risk_reason: Framework labels are not public-source evidence of judgment and cannot be evaluated against the lens.

anti_signals.anti_signal: Treating 'the Bain Way' or any internal method as a documented official standard.
anti_signals.risk_reason: The lens contains public-safe signals only; internal methods and evaluation standards are not public.

anti_signals.anti_signal: Describing impact only as a deliverable or slide deck, without evidence of client adoption or lasting change.
anti_signals.risk_reason: Bain frames results that last and client advocacy, not output volume; this is a preparation signal, not an official disqualifier.

anti_signals.anti_signal: Presenting a polished recommendation while unable to explain the alternatives considered or what evidence would change it.
anti_signals.risk_reason: Bain's hiring process points to objective scoring and case-style problem solving, which reward visible reasoning over a memorized answer.

anti_signals.anti_signal: Treating disagreement as a relationship problem rather than a source of better thinking.
anti_signals.risk_reason: Bain publicly pairs teamwork and trust with tolerance for diverging opinions.

interview_patterns.pattern: Use cited public source signals to test role-relevant judgment, ownership, communication, and impact.

Hiring signals in this lens are derived interview-preparation suggestions: they translate public company positioning into questions a candidate can prepare for, and are not evidence that the company evaluates candidates on them.

honest_limits: This is a lightweight public-source lens and does not represent an official Bain & Company hiring standard.
It contains source metadata and non-verbatim public-safe signals only.
Role, team, seniority, location, and hiring manager can materially change interview emphasis.
This lens requires deeper multi-source validation before being promoted to FULLY_DISTILLED.
